subject: Data boundary options & action plan (Dedicated vs Private VPC)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@medtechinc.com>, Peter Nguyen <peter.nguyen@medtechinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment chat — Data boundary options & action plan

Hi Olivia / Peter — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we all have the same baseline and clear next steps.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary requirement: all PHI and identifiable PII must not leave MedTech-controlled network/tenancy without explicit exception.
- Secondary: Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) preferred for any persisted artifacts.
- Acceptance: If we can demonstrably guarantee crypto + network controls, MedTech will consider Dedicated capacity; otherwise Private (VPC-onboarding or on-prem) is required.

High-level options (short):
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs) + VPC peering: our runtime runs in Redwood-owned tenancy but traffic is routed via customer-controlled ingress (VPC peering / private endpoint). Data-in-transit stays over the peering link and we support prefix/KV cache residency controls. Requires: customer KMS integration for persisted caches and explicit egress policy enforcement.
2) Redwood Private (customer VPC with Redwood control plane or on-prem): compute runs in your VPC or inside your environment. Customer retains full network boundary and KMS. Better fit where regulations forbid any outbound persistence or third-party tenancy.

Attachments included: medtech-network-diagram.pdf (first draft of how peering could look), sow-redwood-medtech-v1.docx (commercial + workplan), soc2-snapshot-2026-06.pdf (high-level compliance snapshot).

Open items / asks from MedTech
- Clarify whether any tokens/inputs can be logged or cached outside your VPC in encrypted form (yes/no).
- Confirm KMS preference: AWS KMS with key policy vs HSM — we'll map integration effort.
- Timeline constraints for procurement and security review.

Proposed next steps (we can execute in parallel)
- Technical deep-dive (SE + infra): 60–90m to validate peering/KMS flows and finalise network diagram — target week of 9/13. (Action: Karthik)
- Legal / Procurement: sign SOW for discovery + pilot (2–3 weeks) — Ben to coordinate.
- Security evidence: we’ll push full SOC2 and architecture diagrams; please list additional artifacts you need.

If you confirm the answers to the open items above I’ll book the SE deep-dive.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Ben — great recap, thanks. We reviewed this with Security and Compliance overnight. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) No persisted PHI/PII is allowed outside our VPC in any recoverable plaintext or unescrowed ciphertext. Short-lived caches inside Redwood are acceptable only if the cache is encrypted with our KMS and keys never leave our control.
2) We prefer Private deployment (customer VPC with Redwood control plane) because our audit policy currently forbids compute in third-party tenancies for production workloads. Dedicated could be acceptable for a non-prod or pilot if the KMS integration and network egress controls are fully vetted.
3) We need a short PII flow diagram (where tokens travel, where ephemeral cache might exist, where logs land) — can you produce this before the SE deep-dive?
4) SOC2 snapshot looks fine; please also include evidence of key rotation processes and logs for encryption material access.

Timeline: procurement aims to have contracting sign-off by early October (10/08) if the SOW and technical evidence are satisfactory.

Next meeting: SE deep-dive preferred 9/14 or 9/15 afternoon CET.

Thanks,
Olivia Grant
VP Product, MedTech Inc.

Internal note — copying key technical distinctions and what I’ll prepare for the deep-dive: 

Short checklist (what we must prove during SE call)
- KMS: demonstrate envelope encryption flow where root key is customer-managed. Show that cache persistence (if any) is wrapped with customer key and KMS calls occur from inside customer VPC or via customer-controlled endpoints.
- Network: show packet flow for VPC peering, private ENIs, and ensure there are no public egress hops. Include expected CIDR rules and NAT behavior.
- Logs: where audit logs land; we must confirm no plaintext request/response stored in Redwood-managed S3 for production. For Dedicated pilot we can offer a narrow retention window and key-wrapped blobs.
- Failover / fallback: how we handle degraded capacity — if Dedicated becomes unavailable we need an explicit fallback that does not move data to a third-party tenancy.
- Attestation: propose a short 'custody' checklist we can sign that maps each requirement to a technical control.

Deliverables I will prepare before 9/14 call:
- PII flow diagram (1 page)
- KMS sequence diagram (1 page)
- Network peering diagram (update medtech-network-diagram.pdf)
- Short tech note on retention/eviction behavior for prefix/KV caches

Estimates: ~2 SE hours to prepare artifacts + 90m deep-dive session. I’ll also list any Redwood infra changes required for a pilot (should be minimal: config + team signoffs).

1) SE deep-dive: book for 2026-09-14 at 15:00 CET (90m) — Karthik + two infra engineers. I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm.
2) Pre-call artifacts: Karthik will send PII flow diagram, KMS sequence, and updated network diagram by EOD 9/11.
3) Legal / SOW: I’ve attached the draft SOW (sow-redwood-medtech-v1.docx). If you can confirm commercial points (term, pilot scope, invoicing) we’ll try to target signature by 10/08.
4) Evidence: SOC2 + key rotation notes will be uploaded to the shared Drive link; we’ll add a short attestation doc for retention and eviction semantics.

Acceptance criteria we’ll use to qualify Dedicated vs Private for production:
- If customer KMS + network egress guarantees are implementable and auditable, Dedicated can be approved for production.
- If policy requires compute inside customer tenancy, we’ll recommend Private (VPC / on-prem) and scope migration steps.
